planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost with bottom heat, since Capsicum baccatum germinates slowly; transplant only after nights stay reliably warm.

directions: Aji Mango is a newer selection within the aji (Capsicum baccatum) group, prized for tapered two- to three-inch pods that ripen from green through orange to red and deliver a distinctly sweet, tropical, mango-like fruitiness ahead of a moderate, lingering heat. Grow it exactly as you would other baccatum types: rich, well-drained soil, full sun, and even moisture, since the plants can turn woody and less productive if allowed to dry out repeatedly between waterings. The sprawling, heavily-branched bushes benefit from staking or a tomato cage once loaded with fruit, and picking ripe pods regularly keeps new flowers setting through a long warm season. In frost-free zones the plant can be overwintered and will return as a short-lived perennial, producing an even heavier crop in its second year.
sources: Trade Winds Fruit — Capsicum baccatum Variety Collection
New Mexico State University Chile Pepper Institute — Aji Pepper Varieties

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost on a heat mat, since chinense seed is slow and erratic to germinate; transplant once nights are reliably warm.

directions: NuMex Suave Orange was bred at the New Mexico State University Chile Pepper Institute as a companion to NuMex Suave Red, combining the classic wrinkled, lantern-shaped habanero pod and citrusy, apricot-toned chinense aroma with almost none of the heat, typically measuring under a thousand Scoville units. The plump pods ripen from green to a rich orange over a long, warm growing season, so give plants the full run of summer and avoid letting nighttime temperatures dip into the 50s while fruit is setting. Because so little capsaicin is present, cooks can use whole or pureed pods generously in salsas, marinades, and fruit-forward hot sauces to capture authentic habanero flavor without overwhelming heat. Rich, well-drained soil and consistent watering through fruit set keep yields high on the compact, bushy plants.
sources: New Mexico State University Chile Pepper Institute
New Mexico State University Cooperative Extension

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost with bottom heat; the weeping, vining growth habit benefits from a cage or trellis once fruit weighs the branches down.

directions: Brazilian Starfish is a Peruvian aji type domesticated in Brazil and grown chiefly for its unusual flattened, deeply-lobed pods that flare out into a five- or six-pointed star shape as they mature from green to red. The flavor is floral and fruity with a medium heat in the 15,000-20,000 Scoville range, similar in punch to a serrano but with the tropical fruitiness typical of Capsicum baccatum. Plants have a lax, weeping, almost vine-like habit rather than the upright form of most peppers, so light staking or a small cage keeps the fruit-laden branches off the ground. Sliced starfish-shaped pods are a striking addition to pickle jars, salsas, and salads; consistent moisture and rich soil produce the heaviest pod set over a long warm season.
sources: Pepper Geek — Brazilian Starfish Pepper Growing Guide
Trade Winds Fruit — Capsicum baccatum Variety Collection

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; harvest at the red stage for drying and grinding into chili flakes or powder, the pepper's primary use in Chinese and Southeast Asian kitchens.

directions: Goat Horn is a long, tapered cayenne-type Capsicum annuum whose curved, horn-shaped four- to six-inch pods ripen from green to a deep orange-red and carry a robust 20,000-50,000 Scoville heat with a bright, fruity edge. Despite its popularity in Sichuan and other Southeast Asian cooking, the variety traces to the Caribbean and grows vigorously in any warm-season garden with full sun and well-drained, fertile soil. Plants are heavy bearers of thin-walled pods that dry quickly on or off the plant, making Goat Horn a good choice for home-ground chili flakes, infused oils, and the toasted whole dried chiles used in stir-fries. Space plants to allow good airflow and stake tall specimens, since a fully loaded plant can carry dozens of pods at once.
sources: Sandia Seed Company — Goat Horn Pepper
